$comment: Rewrites are ordered and the catch-all must stay last, or every route below
The /story rule is dynamic rendering: this is a client-rendered SPA, so a
crawler that does not run JavaScript sees an empty shell. Googlebot renders
JS on a slow second pass; Bingbot, which is what Edge search uses, largely
does not. Crawler agents are therefore proxied to the API, which returns the
Google supports this and does not treat it as cloaking provided the served
content matches what a person sees. That is a rule, not a detail: if the API
page and the SPA page ever diverge in substance, this becomes a penalty.
The long-term answer is SSR for public routes, which is a much larger job.
public/sitemap.xml was DELETED on purpose. Vercel resolves the filesystem
before rewrites, so a static file at that path silently wins and the dynamic
